clue.text: What's required is a small container — with case one can't cope

definitions.meaning: a woven holder for carrying things, such as shopping or bread
add the word 'case' and you get the informal term for a person too frazzled to function

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition needs 'case' tacked on: a basket case is someone who cannot cope.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker carrier is a small container, and the idiom 'basket case' describes somebody unable to manage.

clue.text: One single makes composer bit upset

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a bit part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A lone person finds a composer's small piece disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ROLE into ELOR, written after BACH.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is a single person, which the clue calls one single.

clue.text: Without right they change colour filters

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: stainers are people or things that change the colour of something

explanation.surface: Things that alter colour, minus a right, act as filters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: STAINERS goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sieves and colanders that separate solids from liquids are filters.

clue.text: Flat race doesn't end in time

indicators.note: the race word is not allowed to finish with the letter for time, so that letter is dropped from its end

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A level race that doesn't finish in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't end in' removes the closing T (time) from EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something level and smooth is flat, as an even surface is.

clue.text: In China you go in to it to get out of it

definitions.text: In China you go in to it to get out of it

parts.words: In China you go in to it to get out of it
parts.note: a place in old Chinese cities that people entered in order to get 'out of it', meaning intoxicated on a narcotic drug

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of it' is slang for stoned; the place you enter is where the drug was smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A den where the poppy-derived narcotic was smoked is a place to get out of it.

clue.text: Stealing fish? One's in hot water!

definitions.meaning: taking fish or game illegally from someone else's land
the cooking method where food, such as an egg, is simmered in hot water

explanation.walkthrough: 'In hot water' suggests trouble, which suits the thief, but it is the cooking method.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking game illegally and cooking gently in simmering liquid share one word.

clue.text: Like bare floorboards etc. Pure and new

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Floorboards, et cetera, are pure and new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ETC, PURE and AND, ten letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Floorboards with no rug or fitted covering are bare, without carpet.

clue.text: Tennis scorecard

definitions.meaning: a playing card with the number two

explanation.definitionFit: Forty-all in tennis and the two in a deck of cards share one word.

clue.text: See 19
Swipes back chair

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to swipe is to steal, or loot

explanation.surface: Someone steals the back of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses LOOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat without arms or back is a simple kind of chair.

clue.text: Dog opening present

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a rent is a tear or gap

explanation.surface: A dog opening a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means present, of now.

clue.text: Judge Bill

explanation.definitionFit: To account means to reckon or deem, and an invoice is a bill.

clue.text: Dwell over what's horrible

indicators.note: over signals the word is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: to dwell is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Lingering on something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is what's horrible.

clue.text: Mum gets formal fine in this Scottish town

parts.note: the formal word for mum
feeling fine is being well

explanation.surface: A mother is formally fine in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTHERWELL is a town in Lanarkshire, near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherwell is a town in North Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Large sum of money starts to entice state's corrupt rulers

parts.note: a pot is a large sum, as in 'pots of money'

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word entice are taken, its first two
corrupt means the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: the word state, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A fortune and enticements start to make a state's rulers corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes EN from 'entice'; 'corrupt' turns STATE into TATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Potentates are monarchs or powerful rulers.

clue.text: Fur sent back to the French company

indicators.note: sent back means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Fur sent back to the French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses TO+LE+CO, giving OC+EL+OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat whose pelt was prized as fur.

clue.text: New nurse is without means

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: taken as written
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A new nurse has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: IS goes round N+TEND. 'means' looks like money but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to mean, have in mind.

clue.text: Leave upset sailor and soldier

parts.note: to desert is to leave

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Abandoning a sailor and a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TAR into RAT. Desert Rats was the nickname of British troops in North Africa in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier in Britain's 7th Armoured Division.

clue.text: Go mad over slaughtered deer's stole

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the word upside down

parts.note: to flip is to go mad

indicators.note: slaughtered means the letters are cut up and rearranged

parts.note: the word deer, the 's standing for 'has'

explanation.surface: Going mad over slaughtered deer's fur wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns FLIP into PILF; 'slaughtered' turns DEER into ERED. 'stole' looks like a fur wrap but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilfer is to steal small things, so pilfered means stole.

clue.text: Go for it, weed!

parts.note: an urging to tackle something hard boldly, put as an order to take hold of a stinging plant

explanation.walkthrough: The stinging weed stings less if gripped firmly, hence the idiom for facing a difficulty head on.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a difficulty boldly is to go for it.

clue.text: One like a hermit, primarily silent with sour exterior

indicators.note: the sour word forms an exterior, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: acetic means sour, like vinegar

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of silent

explanation.surface: A hermit-like person, mostly silent, with a sour outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives S, which goes inside ACETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic lives a life of strict self-denial, as a hermit does.

clue.text: One cuts out corns with end of knife

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order
end of picks the last letter of knife

explanation.surface: Someone removes corns with the tip of a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNS plus E (end of knife) rearranged. 'cuts out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor removes passages from books or films, so is one who cuts.

clue.text: Snag caused by this old Roman trophy

parts.note: hic is Latin for 'this', the language of the old Romans
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A setback caused by an ancient Roman trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor setback or snag.

clue.text: The hangman's craft

definitions.meaning: Jack ... was a notorious English executioner of the 1600s, whose name came to mean any hangman

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like the hangman's trade, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch is the byname of the hangman, and a two-masted sailing vessel shares the name.

clue.text: I defined it, cryptically, as "sympathised"

indicators.note: cryptically means the letters are to be read in a disguised arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have defined a word as sympathised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' rearranges the ten letters of I DEFINED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify with someone is to feel for them, to sympathise.

clue.text: Some generator of love poetry

indicators.note: some means part of the following word, so letters within it are taken

explanation.surface: A source of romantic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Muse is in the middle of 'generator', and she herself is a generator of love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, so she inspires it.

clue.text: Not quite a national flag

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short, losing its last

parts.note: a national of Ireland is Irish

explanation.surface: Not quite a nation's flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a plant: the yellow flag is a wild iris, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a name for several irises, plants with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Competent sounding murder victim

indicators.note: sounding means the clue word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A competent-sounding murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable, competent.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by another Alice character

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland, a book where the White Rabbit also appears

explanation.surface: The White Rabbit is caught by another Alice character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' suggests the White Rabbit, but it is the verb: in British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit, in British slang, is to talk at length, which is to chatter.

clue.text: Show features nude in naughty act

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
naughty means the letters misbehave, coming out of order

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: A show that includes nudity in a risqué act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' turns ACT into CAT, and BARE goes inside after CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment, a show at a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Around lido, pose here

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: People pose here around the lido.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' rearranges LIDO and POSE; the whole clue says where people pose at a lido.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of a swimming pool is where people lounge and show themselves off.

clue.text: A little car's something that crawls

definitions.meaning: the Volkswagen ..., a small rounded car
an insect with hard wing cases

explanation.definitionFit: Volkswagen's small rounded car and a hard-shelled insect share one name.
